summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was readmitted the day after discharge due to recurrent severe epigastric pain, nausea, and constipation unrelieved by oral medications. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and TPN restart. Pain was controlled with IV and transitioned to oral hydromorphone, with the fentanyl patch reduced to 100 mcg/hr. She tolerated oral medications for two days prior to discharge and required no IV medications in the final 24 hours. An MRCP showed stable chronic pancreatitis changes without new pathology. Constipation was managed with her home bowel regimen plus additional doses. She remained on her baseline psychiatric and GERD medications. No infectious source was found. She was discharged home with TPN, home health support, and follow-up arranged with her GI doctor and a new pain clinic consultation to address opioid dependence.
